title: Multi-Cancer Early Screening with Non-contrast CT and Deep Learning.
summary: PANDA reports high pancreatic-lesion detection performance across large CT cohorts, including higher sensitivity and specificity than average radiologists.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Alibaba DAMO reports validation involving 6,239 patients across ten centers and another cohort of 20,530 patients. The source states that PANDA exceeded mean radiologist sensitivity by 34.1% and specificity by 6.3% for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma identification. Survival gains and individual treatment outcomes remain unreported.
purpose: Improve early cancer detection from non-contrast CT images.

ratings.reason: The study reports detection performance, but does not quantify treatment, health, or survival improvements for the people screened.
PANDA reportedly exceeds mean radiologist sensitivity by 34.1% and specificity by 6.3% for pancreatic cancer identification in the evaluated cohorts.
Lives saved and population screening benefits are asserted downstream possibilities.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 27: Multi-Cancer Early Screening with Non-contrast CT and Deep Learning.

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: PANDA reports strong pancreatic-cancer detection in CT studies
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
